full_judgment:
2. The short fact necessary for disposal of this appeal is that appellant Nos. 1 and 2 and respondent No. 20 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 43 of 1996 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, first Court. Khulna (now Joint District Judge) for redemption or the mortgage property along with other reliefs on the averments. inter-alia that plaintiff No. 1 is a private limited company constituted by the shares having its head office at Mirerdanga under Police Station Daulatpur within District Khulna. Plaintiff Nos.2-3 and defendant Nos.5-6 are the son, the daughter and the wives respectively of late Sirajul Islam Khan, Managing Director of plaintiff No. 1: defendant Nos. 1-2 are the banking company Defendant No. 1 sanctioned loan of TK. 7,14,000.00 and TK. 1,75,000.00 on 28-12-1970 as per prayer or plaintiff No. I for establishing an automatic brick factory. Defendant No. 1 sanctioned further amount of loan in favour of plaintiff No.1 on several occasions. Plaintiff No.1 mortgaged all its movable and immovable properties in favour of defendant No.1 as security against the repayment of the loan. Plaintiff No. 1 failed to repay the loan money, as a result defendant No. 1 attached all the mortgaged properties of plaintiff No. 1 through Court in Miscellaneous Case No.4 of 1974. Sirajul Islam Khan, Managing Director of Plaintiff No. 1 died on 11-11-1979. After the death of Sirajul Islam Khan Plaintiff No.3 was appointed guardian of plaintiff No.2 through GA Case No. 86 of 298 Plaintiffs repaid the loan money to defendant No. 1 and as such they were entitled to redeem the mortgaged property with mesne profit. 

 12. The learned Joint District Judge rejected the application of the defendants on the finding, inter-alia that the plaintiffs filed the suit for redemption of the mortgaged property along with other prayers claiming themselves to be the share-holders of plaintiff No. 1 company and the suit being at the stage of peremptory hearing and an issue as to the maintainability of the suit having already been framed it would not be proper to give decision only on the ground of its maintainability. The learned Joint District Judge further observed that it would require evidence in order to find out the claim of the defendants. In the same order the learned Joint District Judge also took the view that the issue of maintainability of the suit would be decided at the time of its final disposal along with the other issues. The learned District Judge affirmed the order of the learned Joint District Judge with the observation that if the plaint was not properly signed or verified, the Court had jurisdiction to allow the plaintiff to remove the defect at a later stage. The District Judge also observed that the question of maintainability of a suit should be raised at the earlier stage of the proceeding and all the issues should be decided together keeping in view of the evidence and the facts and circumstances of the case. The learned District Judge further observed that the suit was not also barred by any law either expressly or impliedly. 

 14. In the backdrop of the facts and circumstances of the case, the findings given by the High Court Division and the leave granting order. we shall examine first whether the High Court Division was correct in rejecting the prayer for amendment of the plaint on the view that if prayer for amendment was allowed it would change the nature and character of the suit, The issue of amendment of the plaint was not either before the trial Court or before the District Judge. It is a new phenomenon which cropped up before the High Court Division during the pendency of the civil revision. It is by now a well settled legal proposition that amendment of the plaint can be allowed at any stage of the proceedings provided (a) amendment, if allowed, would not change the nature and character of the suit or the plaint (b) amendment is necessary far the purpose of determining the real question in controversy between the parties and (c) amendment if allowed would in no way cause injustice to the adverse party. Amendment of the plaint as sought for has been quoted hereinbefore, a reading of which it appears that by the proposed amendment the plaintiff sought for striking out the name of plaintiff No. 1 from the category of plaintiff and to implead it as a defendant and to renumber plaintiff Nos. 2-4 as plaintiff Nos. 1-3. By the proposed amendment the plaintiff's also sought to delete the statements made in the plaint as regard to their claim of becoming the director of the company after the death of its Managing Director, Sirajul Islam Khan and to delete the statements made in the plaint to the effect the plaintiff No. 1 mortgaged all its movable and immovable properties to defendant No. 1 and to insert the new facts to the effect that the properties of Sirajul Islam Khan were mortgaged to defendant No. 1 and after the death of Sirajul Islam Khan plaintiff Nos. 2 and 3 and defendant Nos. 5 and 6 became his heirs. 

 16. Now coming to the question as to whether the High Court Division was justified in rejecting the plaint. As already stated hereinbefore, the learned Advocates of both the parties made the submissions before the High Court Division on the wrong premise that the application filed by the defendants was one under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code, and the learned Judges also proceeded in the same wrong premise and rejected the plaint. At the time of hearing of the leave petition by this Court Mr Nurul Amin also made submissions assuming the application filed by the defendants as one under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code and leave was granted accordingly. Since the learned Judges of the High Court Division treated the application filed by the defendants for dismissal of the suit as one under Order VII, rule 11, of the Code, let us see whether in the facts and the circumstances of the case as disclosed in the plaint as well as in the application, any of the situations as contemplated in the rule was at all attracted warranting rejection of the plaint. 

 17. Order VII, rule 11 of the Code has clearly spelt out that a plaint shall be rejected (a) where the plaint does not disclose any cause of action (b) where relief claimed is undervalued. and the plaintiff on being required by the Court to correct the valuation within a time to be fixed by the Court fails to do so (c) where the relief claimed is properly valued. but the plaint is written upon a paper institfficiently stamped, and the plaintiff, on being required by the Court to supply the requisite stamp-paper within a time to be fixed by the Court fails to do so and (d) where the suit appears from the statement in the plaint to barred by any law. In the instant case a perusal of the plaint clearly shows that facts constituting cause of action have been stated. In paragraphs 21 and 22 it has been stated when the cause of action arose to file the suit. In the application no question was raised as regards the valuation of the suit as well as the non-payment of insufficient Court fees. From the statements made in the plaint it does not appear to us that the suit is barred by any law. The only claim of the defendants on which they sought to dismiss the suit was that the plaintiff No. 1 company was not properly represented and the other plaintiffs being neither Directors of the company nor its Share-holders had right to represent the company, In the plaint it was categorically stated that after the death of Sirajul Islam Khan. Managing Director of the company, plaintiff Nos. 2 and 3 being his son and wife became the directors of the company and as such they were entitled to redeem the mortgaged property. The plea taken by the defendants in the application that none of the said plaintiffs have got 5000 shares to become the director of the company nor the company approved them to be share-holders of the company are purely question of fact which shall have to be thrashed out on the basis of the evidence to be produced by the parties at the time of hearing of the suit particularly the suit being at the stage of peremptory hearing. Considering the statements made in the plaint as well as in the application it appears to us that none of the situations as contemplated in Order VII. rule11 of the Code was attracted. It is true that the provisions of rule 11 are not exhaustive in the matter or rejection of plaint and in exceptional situation aplaint can be rejected under section 151 of the Code even if it does not come within the mischief of this rule, but such situation is absent in the instant case. It is also a fact that the application for dismissal of the suit was filed after about 9 (nine) years from the date of filing of the suit when the same was at the stage of peremptory hearing. The very filing of the application at such a belated stage particularly when the suit was fixed for peremptory hearing does not show bonafide on the part of defendants. It appears to us that the application was filed just to delay the disposal of the suit. In the above context, the learned Joint District Judge while rejecting the application rightly observed that an issue as to the maintainability having already been framed, the same shall be decided along with other issues the learned District Judge rightly affirmed the said view of the learned Joint District Judge, but the learned Judges of the High Court Division totally failed to consider the above discussed factual and legal aspect of the case as well as observations of the Courts below. The learned Judges themselves having observed that the defect as to the framing of suit ought to have been detected at the earlier stage, they ought not to have allowed the application However, in view of the amendment of the plaint, all the objections raised by the defendants in the application have lost their legal force.
